messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

The error message is a bit misleading, but the associated warnings "The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common." are more informative.

It means there are no chromosomes in common between your differential regions and the annotation. This is often the case if different chromosome naming styles (ensemble, ucsc) are used. You can use the [seqlevelsStyle()](https://rdrr.io/bioc/GenomeInfoDb/man/seqlevelsStyle.html) from the GenomeInfoDb package to check and change the chromosome naming style for your GRanges objects.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: start=end or fixed wiedth
messages.body_plain:
Hi TJ,

The default analysis mode in methylKit will be CpG-base-centric, thus having the same start and end position is expected. The default outcome will be a single differentially methylated cytosine (DMC), not a region (DMR).

However, you may perform regional analysis over regions of interest (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#41_Regional_analysis) or genomic tiles (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#35_Tiling_windows_analysis) to find DMRs.  You can also aggregate neighbouring DMCs with similar levels of methylation difference into DMRs using segmentation (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#57_methSeg():_segmentation_of_methylation_or_differential_methylation_profiles).

Best,
Alex

I know one way to do is to pool the replicate for each site, so I would only have sample per site, but I am not quite certain if that’s the best way to go.

Is there any way to do something like multi-factorial analysis in methylKit, that can take into account the variation in sites and replicates?

I wonder if anyone has done similar experimental and has any advice.

Thank you,

Cen
